moat: Strong brand at the very top (Oberoi: 14 of 15 benchmarked hotels rank 1st or 2nd in their competitive sets; RGI 191 for Oberoi hotels in FY26), irreplaceable owned assets (Vilas resorts, The Oberoi Mumbai and New Delhi, Trident Nariman Point); small scale (~4,200 keys) and slow growth limit the network effect that IHCL enjoys.
critiques: Growth is slow and owned-asset heavy: no new owned keys open in FY27-28 except Visakhapatnam (via the associate) and the Grand's return in Sep-2028; the managed pipeline (1,833 keys) is back-ended to 2029-30 and keeps slipping.
Margins fell in FY26 (37.5% -> 34.8%) and again in Q1FY27 (25.4% vs 27.9%): flight catering mix, airport levy, labour codes, Rajgarh ramp-up, renovation write-offs and a Rs30 cr political donation.

Wildflower Hall (85 keys, one of the group's most profitable resorts) is now owned by the State; EIH runs it only on interim terms while an auction is held. Losing it, or winning at a high revenue share, lowers profit.
Governance: a reported family dispute over the promoter holding, two executive Oberois paid ~Rs16 cr each (465-470x the median employee), a royalty to a promoter company, and a political donation.
Bull case: EIH is the purest listed luxury-hotel asset in India, with net cash, Reliance and ITC on the register, and trades at its lowest multiple in years while IHCL and ITC Hotels trade higher.
gaps: Axis Capital's valuation method, multiple, estimate year and estimates are not public; the second analyst in the S&P consensus (target ~Rs350) is not named. Brief and method history say EV/EBITDA; we could not confirm FY28E from a note dated on or before 30-Sep-2026.
No broker FY27E-FY28E estimates found, so the forecasts-vs-street table compares only with our own numbers and the company's history.
Oberoi Flight Services annual revenue and margin are not disclosed (quarterly revenue only on calls); Rajgarh revenue not disclosed; management fees not disclosed.
Wildflower Hall's revenue and profit under the interim operating arrangement are not disclosed; the auction result was not known at 30-Sep-2026.
FY24 revenue split by stream not collected (AR FY25 not read); streams shown for FY25-FY26 only.
Annual report publication date: the report was filed before the 76th AGM on 7-Aug-2026; exact BSE filing date not captured.
conflicts: FY26 profit before exceptional items: company Rs812 cr (deck slide 22, 'w/o exceptional items & related tax') vs Screener Rs748 cr (reported PAT Rs657 cr + Rs91 cr exceptional after tax). The gap is the tax treatment of the Mashobra items; we use Screener's attributable Rs715 cr (Profit for PE) for the P/E history.
Opening years: the Q1FY27 deck shows The Oberoi Goa in 2028, the annual report 'late 2029'; the MD & CEO said the annual report is the better guide.
Company 'EBITDA' (Rs1,190 cr FY26; Rs207 cr Q1FY27) includes other income; operating EBITDA is Rs1,024 cr / Rs167 cr. All our multiples use operating EBITDA, as Screener and the peers do.
